summary: The FK/reference-helper DMC pilot in Core exposed a repetitive human coordination loop (agent works, human verifies Git, packages evidence, dispatches the next bounded prompt); the workflow-automation concept and consolidated coordinator hypothesis were preserved to address the coordination overhead, not to replace maintainer semantic authority.
notes: Core commits are pre-carve-out incubator history, imported for provenance under docs/imported/core-incubator/.

summary: WFC's executable mechanics (Slices 1 through 5, including the reducer, the Codex adapter, and the trusted Coordinator-owned Git commit boundary) were designed, implemented, and independently reviewed inside the spreadsheet-handling/core incubator before any carve-out.
notes: History preserved by the carve-out; these commits are now part of this repository's own Git history, not only Core's.

summary: The carve-out system-boundary review returned Verdict B (direction sound, specific prerequisites should stabilize first); those prerequisites were closed inside Core, then mechanical extraction (carveout.yaml) produced this standalone repository with imported history.
notes: The composable-product/nested-loop concept (2026-09-18) fixed a still-relevant shape: bounded inner execution (proven) is independent of an optional future outer loop or interactive assistant (neither built).

summary: Standalone bootstrap Slices B1 and B2 were accepted and closed: reusable self-development governance, the Runtime-N/Development-N+1 topology, and the first WFC-on-WFC WorkItem were committed and made ready for maintainer-authorized dogfooding.

The first two WFC-on-WFC self-development attempts ran: Attempt 1 stopped fail-closed on an agent authority/evidence misunderstanding (Contract V2); Attempt 2 completed developer-ergonomics scaffolding and correctly had an invalid Finding-ID delta rejected (Contract V3).
notes: Both stops were the reducer correctly refusing an unauthorized or malformed agent request, not a Coordinator defect.

summary: BUG-WFC-PROFILE-DURABLE-ARTIFACT-INSTANCE-COUPLING: the self-development profile hard-coded one review-artifact filename, so a fresh continuation Run could not get a fresh artifact; preflight correctly failed closed. Fixed by a dedicated per-WorkItem review namespace.
notes: A governance/profile configuration defect, distinct from the agent-contract-projection and test-lifecycle defect classes below.

summary: Attempts 3 and 4 exposed two Agent Operating Contract projection defects: the contract did not tell an agent which phase held Finding-disposition authority (Contract V4), and did not distinguish current-Hop authority from future route-target authority (Contract V5). Both were reducer-enforced correctly; only what was truthfully projected to the agent was wrong.
notes: The reducer never granted authority the agent was not entitled to in either case; each stop was fail-closed.

summary: Three test-lifecycle/test-environment defects surfaced during Attempts 3 and 5-6, unrelated to Coordinator production semantics: an architecture test's ambient-PATH dependency on bare `python`; a permanent test that wrongly encoded a one-time pre-launch state-root absence as a permanent invariant; and a permanent test comparing literal executable-path spelling instead of canonical interpreter identity.
notes: Production _preflight() and the reducer were correct in all three cases; only the tests' own assumptions were fragile.

summary: Attempt 7 completed the developer-ergonomics dogfood workstream in exactly one Hop (rereview -> accept -> completed), no Findings, clean worktree, closing the wave that had exposed and fixed the governance-config, contract-projection, and test-environment defect classes above.
notes: A deferred profile optimization (clean review routing directly to rereview) was deliberately not implemented here; it remains recorded future work.

summary: The first real (non-self-development) consumer Run, RUN-a9f9d68c (WorkItem DMC-RELKEY-C0-S1) against Core, implemented cleanly with passing trusted evidence; independent review found no semantic or scope defect but opened one blocking Finding because the governing Core task required a commit-trailer format CommitIntent could not express.
notes: Recorded as a deferred WFC capability gap (FTR-WFC-COMMIT-INTENT-BODY), not a defect in this run's correctness.

summary: Core DMC-RELKEY-C0 Slices 2 (FK delegation) and 3a (lookup delegation) were implemented and independently accepted, each cited as a governing accepted component for the subsequent Slice-3b Run.
notes: Core-internal work; anchored by Core review paths (relation_key_identity_slice2_fk_delegation_implementation_review_2026-09-25.adoc, relation_key_identity_slice3a_lookup_delegation_implementation_review_2026-09-25_review_002.adoc), not by commit hash captured in this repository.

summary: An autonomous WFC Runtime run (RUN-744364f0, hop budget 6, 4 Hops used) executed DMC-RELKEY-C0-S3B against Core: H001 implemented, H002 independent review found a real BLOCKING DateTime relation-key precision defect (changes_required), H003 corrected it, and H004 independently rereviewed and accepted the corrected state -- one meaningful end-to-end implement/review/correct/rereview convergence in a real consumer repository.
notes: Four Hops produced three commits (H004's acceptance created none); do not infer one commit per Hop. This is empirical confidence from one real run, not a general correctness, safety, or arbitrary-autonomy claim.

summary: The product-boundary concept (WFC is Level-0 governed bounded execution; a Level-1 Higher Loop that decides what work exists next is a different problem class living outside the product) was defined, adversarially reviewed, corrected, delta-rereviewed, and had its remaining findings closed -- see DEC-WFC-004.
notes: Non-normative concept lifecycle; authorizes no implementation, FTR, or Run.

summary: COORDINATOR_HARD_MAX_AUTONOMOUS_HOPS was raised from 5 to 20 and independently accepted, with the WorkItem <= RepositoryPolicy <= Coordinator hard ceiling relationship re-verified as independently enforced at each of its four sites -- see DEC-WFC-007 and DEC-WFC-008.
notes: No configured policy or WorkItem was widened by this change; it enabled the Slice-3b run's hop_limit=6 against whatever Core-facing RepositoryPolicy governed that Run.
